clue.text: Gloomy start for players

definitions.meaning: the first, accented beat of a bar, signalled by a conductor's lowered baton

explanation.definitionFit: A pessimistic mood is called this, and musicians begin a bar on the conductor's lowered stroke of the same name.

clue.text: Unhappy lady belts up!

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a lady's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: lams means hits hard, belts

explanation.surface: An indignant cry telling a sulky woman to fasten her seatbelt, or to shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belts up' reads as a slang order to be quiet, but 'up' reverses the synonym for belts in this down clue; Di is a familiar short form of Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and unhappy are synonyms for gloomy, miserable.

clue.text: Overturn Treasury's initial approval in service dispute — a fine achievement

indicators.note: to overturn is to turn upside down, so in this down clue the whole assembled string is read backwards
initial picks just the opening letter of the word Treasury's
in places the approval word between the letters for service and dispute

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
a row is a quarrel or dispute
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: A government department's backing is reversed in an armed-forces quarrel, and the outcome is a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: T + RAF OK ROW gives TRAFOKROW; 'Overturn' reverses all of it into the answer. The RAF is Britain's air force.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is so called, an accomplishment of great skill and beauty.

clue.text: Start to recover after writer's block

indicators.note: after says the opening letter follows the writer's name

parts.note: J. M. Barrie, the Scottish author of Peter Pan

indicators.note: Start to picks the opening letter of the word recover

explanation.surface: A novelist suffering writer's block is urged to make a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' reads as one phrase, but 'block' alone is the definition and the writer is J. M. Barrie, author of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier blocks the way, an obstruction.

clue.text: Set aside money to support lady patrician

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed underneath holds up the ones above it

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
U means upper-class, as a patrician is
L stands for pound, from libra, a unit of British money

explanation.surface: An instruction to put cash aside to keep an aristocratic woman.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage; L is the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a ruling or marriage is to cancel it, declare it void.

clue.text: Exile from revolutionary regime

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so the letters of regime are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political refugee who fled a regime born of revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigre is a person living abroad, often for political reasons, as an exile does.

clue.text: Distinguished dame, shattered by being dismissed

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of dame are rearranged

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A honoured dame left exhausted after being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distinguished' looks like praise for the dame, but it is the definition, in its sense of seen clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made out something is to have discerned or perceived it.

clue.text: Control of clutch

definitions.meaning: a firm hold or command over something

explanation.definitionFit: A grip on power is control, and to seize with the hand is to clutch.

clue.text: Curse a person in management grade

parts.note: an exec, executive, is a person in management
to rate is to grade, or a rate is a grade

explanation.surface: Swearing at a manager of a certain rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil on, to damn.

clue.text: Impenetrable space — very close!

parts.note: air is open space, as in into thin air
tight means very close, as in a tight finish

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a crowded room with no room at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sealed so that no gas can pass is impermeable, impenetrable.

clue.text: Buccaneer in royal fracas risked torture

indicators.note: to torture is to twist and wrench, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for royal, as in RN, Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A pirate who caused a brawl at court and risked being tortured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torture' rearranges IN, R, FRACAS and RISKED. Drake, the Elizabethan seafarer, raided Spanish ships with royal blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan seafarer plundered Spanish ships and was seen as a pirate by Spain.

clue.text: A party that's hostile to others'

parts.note: a social is an informal party

explanation.surface: A get-together where the guests are unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding or rejecting company, unsociable.

clue.text: Private report from a staunch colleague

indicators.note: report means a sound or the spoken word, so the soldier's title is heard

parts.note: a trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment

explanation.surface: A confidential report written by a loyal fellow worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private report' looks like a confidential document; 'report' is the sound indicator and the private is a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouper is a reliable, uncomplaining stalwart who keeps going, like a veteran actor.

clue.text: Supporting stocking

definitions.meaning: bearing the weight of, holding up
having goods on sale, as a shop does

explanation.definitionFit: Bearing a load is holding it up, and a shop that keeps an item has it in stock.

clue.text: Love in university town's beginning to get complicated

definitions.text: Love in university town's beginning to get complicated

indicators.note: to get complicated is to become tangled, so these letters are mixed up
beginning picks the opening letter of the word town's

explanation.surface: A romance at a college town that soon turns messy.
explanation.walkthrough: LOVE IN plus U and T are rearranged by 'to get complicated'; the result itself means complicated, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Involute means intricate or tangled, literally rolled inward.

clue.text: Start of the retreat from an old woman

indicators.note: Start of picks the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: a rout is a disorderly retreat

explanation.surface: An elderly lady sets off from a place of retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old trout' is a British insult for an unattractive or bad-tempered older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a disagreeable older woman is an old trout.

clue.text: Put down on island that lacks nothing

parts.note: over can mean on, on top of

indicators.note: that lacks means the island's name is missing a letter

parts.note: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia
O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Something laid down on an island where nothing is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: BORNEO without its final O gives BORNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overborne means overwhelmed, suppressed, crushed.

clue.text: Poseurs are disappointing in plays

indicators.note: in places the disappointing word inside the plays word

parts.note: shows are stage plays
off means not up to standard, disappointing

explanation.surface: Pretentious actors give poor performances in theatre productions.
explanation.definitionFit: Show-offs are exhibitionists who strike attitudes, like posers.

clue.text: Appearance of a pillbox perhaps points to hostilities

parts.note: a pillbox is a small round brimless hat
E and S, east and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: Sight of a concrete gun emplacement suggests war.
explanation.walkthrough: A pillbox is also a small concrete gun post, which makes 'hostilities' read as warfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Hates as a plural noun means feelings of hatred, enmities.

clue.text: Colour reproduction of royal castle

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: R stands for royal, as in RN, Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a replica of a royal castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant shade of red.

clue.text: Spoiled through keeping it hot — quite ruined finally

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so it goes into the word for through

parts.note: via means by way of, through

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the three words hot, quite and ruined

explanation.surface: Food overcooked and quite ruined in the end by being kept warm.
explanation.walkthrough: VIA keeping IT gives VITIA; the last letters of 'hot quite ruined' add TED.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitiate is to impair or spoil the quality of something.

clue.text: Everything due to be taken into consideration

parts.note: all means everything
owed means due, payable

explanation.surface: A demand that all debts be taken into account.
explanation.definitionFit: To be allowed for is to be considered, made provision for.

clue.text: New in America, this breed of cattle

definitions.meaning: precede with New to get a US state
a dairy breed from a Channel Island

explanation.surface: An American newcomer belongs to this cattle breed.
explanation.walkthrough: New Jersey is a US state; the island in the English Channel gives its name to a dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state New ___ shares its name with a Channel Island dairy breed.

clue.text: What a dog might do to a bird?

definitions.meaning: a pleased dog shakes its tail from side to side
a small songbird that bobs its rear constantly

explanation.surface: Asks what a dog would do on seeing a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy dog wags its tail, and a slender songbird that bobs its rear has the same name.

clue.text: Verbal pledge to judge

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the pledge word is said aloud

parts.note: a gage is a pledge or token, like a glove thrown down

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a spoken promise to sit in judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To gauge is to estimate or assess, to judge.

clue.text: Strength of character shown by politician in trouble

indicators.note: in puts the politician inside the trouble word

parts.note: care means worry, trouble
a Lib is a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician shows mettle when facing difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means quality or worth of a person, their mettle.

clue.text: Novice in church giving up drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A new churchgoer who has sworn off alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' looks like abstaining but signals reading ALE upwards; a chela is a disciple of a guru.
explanation.definitionFit: A chela is a disciple or pupil of a Hindu guru, a beginner on the path.

clue.text: The language of love and hate, for example

definitions.meaning: bad language, swearing, as in mind your language
both these words have four letters

explanation.definitionFit: Swear words are called this, and love and hate each have just four letters.

clue.text: Not all gypsies take early retirement

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Travellers who stop work and retire early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early retirement' suggests leaving work young; it is going to bed for a nap in the early afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a nap taken in the early afternoon.

clue.text: Tack to starboard initially and go off track

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word starboard

parts.note: eggs that addle go bad, go off
RY, railway, is a track

explanation.surface: Sailing instructions: tack to the right, then wander off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' reads as a sailing move; it is horse gear. RY is a short form for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddlery is riding equipment for horses, known collectively as tack.
